candidates.next_evidence: Separate traffic from average-check contribution in U.S. comps; track franchisee cash flow, promo funding, loyalty active users, beverage mix, and whether value promotions remain margin-accretive.
candidates.node_relation: Direct operator exposure to value menus, loyalty-driven frequency, digital engagement, beverage expansion, and franchisee margin tradeoffs.
candidates.theme_relation: Large global QSR brand whose comparable-sales resilience is tied to affordability perception, loyalty scale, and menu innovation rather than pure price increases.
candidates.why_include: McDonald's is the obvious scale benchmark for the node: if consumers are value-sensitive, its ability to protect traffic through McValue, loyalty, bundles, and beverages sets the reference point for the whole QSR value-war cycle.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify Taco Bell traffic versus ticket, specialty beverage attachment and standalone order mix, loyalty active-user growth, franchisee restaurant-level margin, and whether Pizza Hut weakness dilutes the node exposure.
candidates.node_relation: Direct operator exposure through Taco Bell value perception, menu innovation, digital/loyalty platforms, beverages, and daypart expansion.
candidates.theme_relation: Taco Bell provides a differentiated case study in value-led traffic and frequency, while KFC/Pizza Hut add global and brand-mix complexity.
candidates.why_include: Yum is relevant because Taco Bell appears to be one of the clearest large-chain examples of value plus innovation plus digital engagement; the underappreciated angle is whether beverages and loyalty can create incremental occasions rather than simply discounting existing demand.

candidates.next_evidence: Check customer concentration, net revenue retention, enterprise QSR wins, Punchh/PAR POS attach rates, implementation cycles, and whether software spend is resilient when operators face margin pressure.
candidates.node_relation: Second-order supplier exposure: provides technology infrastructure for QSR loyalty, guest data, ordering channels, and store-level performance improvement.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Restaurant technology / POS, loyalty, payments, back-office software
candidates.theme_relation: If restaurants need loyalty utility, personalized offers, kiosks, delivery/channel optimization, and margin analytics to defend frequency, PAR can be a chokepoint-like software supplier to multi-unit operators.
candidates.why_include: PAR is a less obvious beneficiary because it is not a restaurant concept, but its QSR data and product suite map directly to the node: loyalty growth, super-user frequency, channel mix, and operational optimization.

candidates.next_evidence: Track location growth, gross payment volume, software attach rates, marketing/loyalty adoption, customer churn among small restaurants, and evidence that operators use Toast tools for traffic-positive promotions rather than only payment processing.
candidates.node_relation: Second-order technology exposure for independent and multi-location restaurants needing menu management, loyalty, discounts, online ordering, payments, and guest marketing.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Restaurant technology / POS, payments, digital ordering, loyalty and marketing
candidates.theme_relation: Toast can benefit if restaurants shift from blunt price hikes to data-driven menu engineering, targeted promotions, loyalty programs, and digital ordering workflows.
candidates.why_include: Toast is underappreciated as a value-traffic node because it sells the tools restaurants use to measure demand, run discounts, manage menus, and convert one-time diners into repeat guests.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify independent restaurant case-volume growth, exclusive-brand penetration, gross profit per case, adoption of menu-profit tools, and whether customers use USFD products to launch lower-cost/high-perceived-value menu items.
candidates.node_relation: Supplier exposure to menu-cost management, private/exclusive brands, labor-saving products, product innovation, and operator consulting that can improve perceived value and margins.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Foodservice distribution / restaurant supplier and services
candidates.theme_relation: If operators need to protect value perception while managing elevated food and labor costs, distributors with menu-engineering tools and exclusive products may become second-order beneficiaries.
candidates.why_include: US Foods is less obvious because it is upstream of the restaurant brands, but its exclusive products, Menu Profit Pro/Menu IQ tools, and operator consulting map directly to menu engineering and affordability pressure.

evidence.claim: The National Restaurant Association's 2026 State of the Restaurant Industry highlights uneven traffic, rising costs, tighter household budgets among low- and middle-income consumers, and the need for creativity and technology to deliver value and productivity.
evidence.source_title: 2026 State of the Restaurant Industry | National Restaurant Association

evidence.claim: McDonald's reported Q1 2026 global comparable sales growth of 3.8% and said trailing-twelve-month systemwide sales to loyalty members across 70 loyalty markets exceeded $38 billion.
McDonald's 2025 results release said full-year systemwide sales to loyalty members rose 20% to nearly $37 billion and 90-day active loyalty users rose 19% to nearly 210 million.

Toast describes itself in its 2025 annual report as a cloud-based, all-in-one digital technology platform purpose-built for the restaurant community, with solutions including online ordering, order and pay, marketing, and loyalty.

Toast's POS product materials say restaurants can use loyalty, email, and SMS marketing to help turn shoppers into repeat customers, and that menu pairings, modifier suggestions, and upgrades can populate on terminals and handhelds.

memory_update.text: MCD and YUM remain core direct operators for the value/traffic/menu-pricing node; research should focus on traffic-positive comps, loyalty frequency, beverage incrementality, and franchisee margin health rather than headline same-store sales alone.

PAR and TOST are second-order software enablers for the same node; their relevance comes from loyalty, guest data, digital ordering, menu/promotional controls, and store-level productivity rather than restaurant traffic ownership.

USFD is a supplier-side hypothesis: foodservice distributors with exclusive brands, menu-cost tools, and operator consulting may benefit if restaurants shift from price increases to menu engineering and labor-saving product design.

The node should be tracked using traffic versus ticket, value-platform durability, loyalty active users, promotional intensity, beverage/daypart mix, restaurant-level margins, and supplier/software attach rates.

Need a separate pass for public data providers and payments players such as credit-card processors, foot-traffic analytics, and delivery marketplaces; they may reveal traffic trends but were not prioritized in this five-candidate expansion.

node: Consumer value, traffic, and menu-pricing power
summary: Expanded the universe around the node where restaurant winners defend frequency and perceived value without relying only on menu inflation. The most relevant public-market mapping includes direct operators with visible value/loyalty/beverage engines and second-order enablers that help operators engineer menus, run loyalty programs, improve digital ordering, or manage food/labor-cost pressure. This is a research universe only, not a ranking or trading recommendation.
